taxonomic_note: Accepted Chinese tallow species; historical Sapium sebiferum and Croton sebifer are synonyms of this taxon, not separate learner cards. Native to Asia and introduced/invasive in Texas.
look_here_first: Check alternate diamond-shaped leaves with a long tapering tip and nearly smooth margins; inspect the leaf-blade base for small glands. Then look for slender flower spikes or a 3-lobed capsule that opens to three bright white wax-coated seeds.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Master Plant Pool source membership; crew identification comparison
project_inclusion.range_basis: Completed deep review and Texas A&M Forest Service/NPSOT treat Chinese tallow as introduced and invasive in Texas; not a native target-zone species.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Presence in Texas, naturalization, and invasive occurrence do not establish native target-zone range.

best_field_traits: Deciduous tree with alternate, simple, broadly rhombic to triangular-ovate leaves
Leaves often have an elongated pointed tip, smooth to nearly smooth margin, and long slender petiole
Small glands near junction of petiole and leaf blade may be visible on close inspection
Terminal yellow-green flower spikes with numerous small flowers
Three-lobed/three-chambered capsules; opening fruit exposes three white waxy seeds resembling popcorn
Autumn leaves can turn red or yellow, but color is not diagnostic
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Texas redbud has cordate leaves and pea-family pods rather than three-lobed capsules with white waxy seeds. Cottonwood/poplar seedlings have toothed triangular leaves and cottony seeds rather than popcorn-like white waxy seeds. Confirm leaf-base glands and fruit whenever possible.

confused_with: young native trees with triangular leaves
comparisons.key_distinctions: Rhombic entire leaves plus paired petiole-base glands and 3-part capsules exposing white waxy seeds identify Chinese tallow; redbud pods and cottonwood catkins/cottony seeds are structurally different.
